summary: 75-ft surplus Navy steel tower and cabin, built 1948 on Gunderson Mtn north of Forks WA; gone by 1969; summit now used for radio. Great Forks Fire lookout 1951.

facts.design: 75-foot surplus Navy steel tower with a cabin on top and a 14x18-foot ground house below
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin gone by 1969 per the register and WillhiteWeb; the summit now has communication structures and an amateur radio repeater is moving there (2020)

staffing.status: named lookouts from 1951 and for 1955-1956 and 1961-1965 in the sources read; no staffing after 1965 found

access.note: WillhiteWeb says a Rayonier recreation permit is required to recreate legally on the timber land beside the gated road.

visit.trail_note: A DNR public access road leads to a gated road toward the summit; WillhiteWeb describes the Rayonier permit requirement on the land beside it

events.note: Road to the lookout site cleared and built before winter so the installation could be finished before the 1948 fire season
75-foot surplus Navy steel tower with a 14x18-foot ground house erected; first radio communication in the area
Great Forks Fire: overnight lookout Glen S. Merchant saw the glow about 18 miles northwest of Forks and reported it to the district warden; fire started at Camp Creek from the Sol Duc fire remains
Nancy Gorbin named as lookout for 1955 and 1956
Beth Velie named as lookout; she describes the cab and ladder
Linda (Fisk) Pickering named for the summers of 1964 and 1965; 1964 newspaper item lists Gunderson among seven lookouts to be manned that June
Last named lookout in the sources read: Linda (Fisk) Pickering
Tower and cabin gone and dismantled by 1969
Registered January 11, 2012 as FFLOS US 1184, WA 85; nominated by Ray Kresek
Clallam County Amateur Radio Club preparing three new antennas for a repeater moving to the site; Forks Community Hospital is the leaseholder

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1,235 ft (376 m). WillhiteWeb and the Forks Forum give 1,200 ft. The brief's 376.4 m is kept, since it matches the register and the difference is rounding in the other sources.
Beth Velie remembered a cab about 10 by 10 feet; Linda Pickering described a 7-foot square viewing cab. The story reports both recollections and does not choose between them.
The register and the Forest Fire Lookout Association give 1948 as the build year. The road was cleared in 1947 for that installation, so the story dates the work to 1947 and 1948.

notes_for_editor: Strongest of the three: several independent accounts (register, FLA listing, WillhiteWeb with Annual Report and newspaper quotes, Forks Forum 2020) agree on the 1948 tower and the 1969 removal. Height 22.9 m is converted from 75 ft. The brief's kind 'tower' and agency match the sources. Staffing rows come from WillhiteWeb recollections and a 1964 newspaper item, not a Forest Service roster, so the story presents them as named lookouts in the sources rather than a full staffing history. The 2020 repeater line is one newspaper item; no later confirmation was read. The brief's record is correct; no corrections. The 2017/2018 drone photo captions are not used as evidence.
